## `N-c-011`: Schild's ALC/modal correspondence
### `N-c-011.a` Klaus Schild (1991)

**Reader-facing delivery and topic review completed, 2026-08-22.** The N-c-011 presentation preserves the source's empty-set convention; reproduces the separate printed role production with only \(R\) as its §3 role metavariable; and discloses both its eliminable atomic-role normalization and the handbook's exact replacement of Schild's domain \(D\) and extension function \(\mathcal E\) by \(I\), \(\Delta^I\), and \((\cdot)^I\). It defines every modal connective and validity notation before use, types both syntactic directions and semantic model constructions, supplies the source-omitted induction as a handbook proof, restores both source examples and all three Lemma 1 reductions, and gives the complete two-world evaluation. Proposition 1 now uses a nonconflicting metalinguistic generator set defined exactly as ordered pairs and a least generated congruence; Proposition 2 states Schild's log-space many-one convention and remains separate from the following quadratic-space sentence. The overview restricts the modal correspondence to standalone concepts with neither TBox nor ABox input and consistently withholds the unacquired arbitrary-TBox classification. 1. **The Vardi--Wolper translation theorem loses the source's own attribution.**  In `handbook/parts/p09/presentations/n-c-013.tex:85-95`, Theorem 2.1 is presented simply as the paper's theorem, and `handbook/parts/p09/logic-in-computer-science.tex:746-750` strengthens that presentation to “Vardi--Wolper's literal Theorem 2.1 bound.”  The controlling source note records that the paper itself attributes Theorem 2.1 to WVS83 (`spec/research/p09-vardi-wolper-1986-source-note.md:114-128`).  Appendix B does supply the preprint's compact construction, so the repair is not to remove Vardi--Wolper or Appendix B; it is to preserve both facts at once: the preprint states the theorem and gives the appendix construction, while explicitly attributing the theorem to WVS83.  The proof-boundary summary at `n-c-013.tex:416-420` should likewise not enumerate the paper's externally cited results while silently omitting this attribution.

2. **The semi-determinism citation omits the location that supports its claimed later use.**  `handbook/parts/p09/presentations/n-c-013.tex:57-60` says that Section 4.4 uses the several-start/single-successor distinction but attaches the locator “preprint p. 4 and app. A.”  The definition is on body p. 4, whereas the use is Lemma 4.6 on body p. 10; Appendix A supplies temporal clauses and automata-connective material, not that Lemma 4.6 use (`spec/research/p09-vardi-wolper-1986-source-note.md:90-112,202-217,442-452`).  The citation must include body p. 10 (or an equivalently exact Lemma 4.6 locator); Appendix A may remain only for claims it actually supports.

3. **The probabilistic complexity bounds use an untyped and source-weakened size parameter.**  `handbook/parts/p09/presentations/n-c-013.tex:211` defines \(\lVert P\rVert\) only for the earlier nonprobabilistic finite-program tuple as its encoded size.  The probabilistic section then introduces the different object \(\Pi=(W,P,w_0,V)\) at `n-c-013.tex:270-287` and reuses \(\lVert P\rVert\) without a new definition in Theorem 4.3 (`n-c-013.tex:348-353`), Theorem 4.5 (`n-c-013.tex:358-381`), and Theorem 4.7 (`n-c-013.tex:383-389`).  The source's exact convention is that these algorithms depend only on which transition probabilities are nonzero and that the finite probabilistic-program size is the number of nonzero transition-matrix entries (`spec/research/p09-vardi-wolper-1986-source-note.md:344-358`).  Define that convention in the probabilistic section and bind all three displayed bounds to it; the earlier generic encoding-size sentence does not type or recover this source claim.

4. **The host theorem assigns effectivity to B\"uchi's Theorem 1 rather than to the paper's later effectivity argument.**  `handbook/parts/p09/logic-in-computer-science.tex:830-845`, especially lines 836-844, says that every relevant formula is “effectively equivalent by B\"uchi's Theorem 1” and then sends closed-sentence truth directly to Lemma 12.  The source boundary is more exact: Theorem 1 states equivalence with a \(\Sigma_1^\omega\) formula; the paper defers the algorithmic strengthening until the later finite-enumeration/effectivity discussion, after which Theorem 2 concludes effective decidability (`spec/research/p09-buchi-1962-source-acquisition.md:338-355,357-399`).  The presentation itself preserves this distinction at `handbook/parts/p09/presentations/n-c-013.tex:670-685,699-728`, so the host currently flattens a boundary that its own cited presentation correctly states.  Split the host sentence accordingly: equivalence comes from Theorem 1, effectiveness from the later effectivity argument, and Lemma 12 supplies the recurrent stem--cycle decision after normalization.

1. **The Vardi--Wolper translation theorem loses the source's own attribution.**  In `handbook/parts/p09/presentations/n-c-013.tex:85-95`, Theorem 2.1 is presented simply as the paper's theorem, and `handbook/parts/p09/logic-in-computer-science.tex:746-750` strengthens that presentation to “Vardi--Wolper's literal Theorem 2.1 bound.”  The controlling source note records that the paper itself attributes Theorem 2.1 to WVS83 (`spec/research/p09-vardi-wolper-1986-source-note.md:114-128`).  Appendix B does supply the preprint's compact construction, so the repair is not to remove Vardi--Wolper or Appendix B; it is to preserve both facts at once: the preprint states the theorem and gives the appendix construction, while explicitly attributing the theorem to WVS83.  The proof-boundary summary at `n-c-013.tex:416-420` should likewise not enumerate the paper's externally cited results while silently omitting this attribution.

2. **The semi-determinism citation omits the location that supports its claimed later use.**  `handbook/parts/p09/presentations/n-c-013.tex:57-60` says that Section 4.4 uses the several-start/single-successor distinction but attaches the locator “preprint p. 4 and app. A.”  The definition is on body p. 4, whereas the use is Lemma 4.6 on body p. 10; Appendix A supplies temporal clauses and automata-connective material, not that Lemma 4.6 use (`spec/research/p09-vardi-wolper-1986-source-note.md:90-112,202-217,442-452`).  The citation must include body p. 10 (or an equivalently exact Lemma 4.6 locator); Appendix A may remain only for claims it actually supports.

3. **The probabilistic complexity bounds use an untyped and source-weakened size parameter.**  `handbook/parts/p09/presentations/n-c-013.tex:211` defines \(\lVert P\rVert\) only for the earlier nonprobabilistic finite-program tuple as its encoded size.  The probabilistic section then introduces the different object \(\Pi=(W,P,w_0,V)\) at `n-c-013.tex:270-287` and reuses \(\lVert P\rVert\) without a new definition in Theorem 4.3 (`n-c-013.tex:348-353`), Theorem 4.5 (`n-c-013.tex:358-381`), and Theorem 4.7 (`n-c-013.tex:383-389`).  The source's exact convention is that these algorithms depend only on which transition probabilities are nonzero and that the finite probabilistic-program size is the number of nonzero transition-matrix entries (`spec/research/p09-vardi-wolper-1986-source-note.md:344-358`).  Define that convention in the probabilistic section and bind all three displayed bounds to it; the earlier generic encoding-size sentence does not type or recover this source claim.

4. **The host theorem assigns effectivity to B\"uchi's Theorem 1 rather than to the paper's later effectivity argument.**  `handbook/parts/p09/logic-in-computer-science.tex:830-845`, especially lines 836-844, says that every relevant formula is “effectively equivalent by B\"uchi's Theorem 1” and then sends closed-sentence truth directly to Lemma 12.  The source boundary is more exact: Theorem 1 states equivalence with a \(\Sigma_1^\omega\) formula; the paper defers the algorithmic strengthening until the later finite-enumeration/effectivity discussion, after which Theorem 2 concludes effective decidability (`spec/research/p09-buchi-1962-source-acquisition.md:338-355,357-399`).  The presentation itself preserves this distinction at `handbook/parts/p09/presentations/n-c-013.tex:670-685,699-728`, so the host currently flattens a boundary that its own cited presentation correctly states. 1. **The Vardi--Wolper translation theorem loses the source's own attribution.**  In `handbook/parts/p09/presentations/n-c-013.tex:85-95`, Theorem 2.1 is presented simply as the paper's theorem, and `handbook/parts/p09/logic-in-computer-science.tex:746-750` strengthens that presentation to “Vardi--Wolper's literal Theorem 2.1 bound.”  The controlling source note records that the paper itself attributes Theorem 2.1 to WVS83 (`spec/research/p09-vardi-wolper-1986-source-note.md:114-128`).  Appendix B does supply the preprint's compact construction, so the repair is not to remove Vardi--Wolper or Appendix B; it is to preserve both facts at once: the preprint states the theorem and gives the appendix construction, while explicitly attributing the theorem to WVS83.  The proof-boundary summary at `n-c-013.tex:416-420` should likewise not enumerate the paper's externally cited results while silently omitting this attribution.

2. **The semi-determinism citation omits the location that supports its claimed later use.**  `handbook/parts/p09/presentations/n-c-013.tex:57-60` says that Section 4.4 uses the several-start/single-successor distinction but attaches the locator “preprint p. 4 and app. A.”  The definition is on body p. 4, whereas the use is Lemma 4.6 on body p. 10; Appendix A supplies temporal clauses and automata-connective material, not that Lemma 4.6 use (`spec/research/p09-vardi-wolper-1986-source-note.md:90-112,202-217,442-452`).  The citation must include body p. 10 (or an equivalently exact Lemma 4.6 locator); Appendix A may remain only for claims it actually supports.

3. **The probabilistic complexity bounds use an untyped and source-weakened size parameter.**  `handbook/parts/p09/presentations/n-c-013.tex:211` defines \(\lVert P\rVert\) only for the earlier nonprobabilistic finite-program tuple as its encoded size.  The probabilistic section then introduces the different object \(\Pi=(W,P,w_0,V)\) at `n-c-013.tex:270-287` and reuses \(\lVert P\rVert\) without a new definition in Theorem 4.3 (`n-c-013.tex:348-353`), Theorem 4.5 (`n-c-013.tex:358-381`), and Theorem 4.7 (`n-c-013.tex:383-389`).  The source's exact convention is that these algorithms depend only on which transition probabilities are nonzero and that the finite probabilistic-program size is the number of nonzero transition-matrix entries (`spec/research/p09-vardi-wolper-1986-source-note.md:344-358`).  Define that convention in the probabilistic section and bind all three displayed bounds to it; the earlier generic encoding-size sentence does not type or recover this source claim.

4. **The host theorem assigns effectivity to B\"uchi's Theorem 1 rather than to the paper's later effectivity argument.**  `handbook/parts/p09/logic-in-computer-science.tex:830-845`, especially lines 836-844, says that every relevant formula is “effectively equivalent by B\"uchi's Theorem 1” and then sends closed-sentence truth directly to Lemma 12.  The source boundary is more exact: Theorem 1 states equivalence with a \(\Sigma_1^\omega\) formula; the paper defers the algorithmic strengthening until the later finite-enumeration/effectivity discussion, after which Theorem 2 concludes effective decidability (`spec/research/p09-buchi-1962-source-acquisition.md:338-355,357-399`).  The presentation itself preserves this distinction at `handbook/parts/p09/presentations/n-c-013.tex:670-685,699-728`, so the host currently flattens a boundary that its own cited presentation correctly states.  Split the host sentence accordingly: equivalence comes from Theorem 1, effectiveness from the later effectivity argument, and Lemma 12 supplies the recurrent stem--cycle decision after normalization.

### `N-c-017.a` Randal E. Bryant (1986)

**Reader-facing delivery status, 2026-08-22.** The function-graph definition and denotation, fixed-order condition, both reductions, a worked reduction, Theorem 1 with its dependency-set induction and conditional minimality, Figure 2's exact eight-versus-sixteen ordering comparison, Figure 7's `Apply` trace, the annotated complexity correction, and the order-independent multiplier lower bound have been reconstructed in `handbook/parts/p09/presentations/n-c-017.tex`. The reconstruction remains strictly at Bryant's Boolean-representation layer; transition systems and CTL enter only under later presentations. Acquisition and reader-facing reconstruction for `N-c-017.a` are **closed at the annotated author version's own strength**. Independent topic reviews, section admission, and the final post-freeze static/build/visual publication pass remain separate and outstanding.

**Reader-facing delivery status, 2026-08-22.** The paper's finite-domain relational μ-calculus and monotonicity condition, mutually recursive BDD evaluator, finite fixed-point convergence, Boolean-domain encoding, exact CTL-to-μ translations, symbolic predecessor operation, a complete `EU` approximation trace, iterative-squaring mechanism and limitation, and the three-stage pipeline's actual register property and empirical figures have been reconstructed in `handbook/parts/p09/presentations/n-c-017.tex`. Bryant's conditional representation theorem remains a separately attributed preceding presentation. Acquisition and reader-facing reconstruction for `N-c-017.b` are **closed at the 1992 article's own strength**. Independent topic reviews, section admission, and the final post-freeze static/build/visual publication pass remain separate and outstanding.

## `N-c-018`: the propositional modal mu-calculus, automata, games, and alternation
### `N-c-018.a` Dexter Kozen (1983)

**Reader-facing delivery status, 2026-08-22.** The N-c-018 presentation now gives the exact 1983 grammar, relational/state-set semantics, ordinal approximants, dual greatest fixed point, source closure, active-variable relation, literal aconjunctive restriction with permitted/excluded examples, continuity counterexample, Propositions 4.1--4.2 and their unequal proof status, axioms and Park induction, all five tableau rules, counter standing and use, four algorithm outcomes, termination proof architecture, Theorem 6.3.1, and its directional proof boundary. The detailed audit is `spec/research/p09-kozen-1983-source-note.md`. Acquisition, visual transcription, and reader-facing reconstruction for N-c-018.a are **closed**. Independent topic reviews, section admission, and the final post-freeze publication pass remain separate and outstanding.
### `N-c-018.b` E. Allen Emerson and Charanjit S. Jutla (1991)

**Reader-facing delivery status, 2026-08-22.** The N-c-018 presentation now gives both automaton tuples and games; Streett/Pairs acceptance; thread, ithread, and both history-free standings; the exact Theorem 2.2 bounds; the source-specific tree semantics; both printed defects; Fischer--Ladner closure; pre-model regeneration; Theorem 3.1's complete printed construction sketch; expressive equivalence and complementation; the largest-recurring parity convention; the exact Theorems 4.1--4.2 formulas; the unequal proof status of Theorems 4.1--4.4; and both §5 applications. The paper itself contains no worked automaton run, small determinization example, complete §§2--3 proofs, or state bound for Theorem 3.1. Those are source limitations, not open reader-facing obligations. Acquisition, visual transcription, and reconstruction for `N-c-018.b` are **closed at the extended abstract's own strength**. Jutla's dissertation remains an optional separately attributed proof-expansion source; independent topic reviews, section admission, and the final post-freeze static/build/visual publication pass remain outstanding.

\begin{hbdefinition}{def:p12-lcf-architecture}{LCF architecture}
An \emph{LCF architecture} is the programming discipline in which values of an
abstract theorem type can be constructed only by a small set of trusted
primitive inference functions, while untrusted tactics compose those

| D-P11-014 | S / should | LCF architecture and de Bruijn criterion | **fill at S**, paired with N-c-038 | LCF's abstract theorem type/kernel discipline and independently checkable proof-object discipline are defined apart; the table never infers the de Bruijn criterion merely from the marketing label “small kernel.” |
